newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish opposition party seeks minister probe.
newsitem.headline: Turkish opposition party seeks minister probe.

text.p: Turkey's chief opposition party on Thursday requested a parliamentary investigation of the interior minister, adding to pressure on the Islamist-led coalition.

The Anatolian news agency said the Motherland Party asked for the probe into claims minister Meral Aksener had abused her position in the removal of national police chief Alaadin Yuksel in a clandestine, overnight sacking last month.
"It is an abuse of duty to start a (new) public official in a post during a night operation which did not conform with the law," said the demand presented to the speaker of parliament's office.

The motion, which must be considered by parliament within a month, could be a fresh test of Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan's coalition with conservatives, which has already weathered a series of similar parliamentary challenges.
Turkish shares plunged 6.85 percent on Thursday morning in doubts about the government's ability to overcome the latest pressure, led by the country's powerful armed forces.
The military-dominated National Security Council in February ordered the government to crack down on what it saw as rising Islamist activism since the coalition came to power last June.
The council is to hold a monthly meeting on Saturday where it is expected to weigh up the government's efforts.

The ruling alliance has in particular been at odds over the military demand for eight years of compulsory education, which Erbakan's Islamist Welfare Party sees as a threat to the influence of religious schools.
According to newspaper reports, Motherland leader Mesut Yilmaz has proposed an alliance with leftists and Tansu Ciller, leader of the coalition's conservative wing, to form a new government.
